subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add native per-token Gateway identity/scopes for token-mode Control UI users, or keep multi-user isolation delegated to trusted-proxy/front-layer deployments for now?
rationale: The request changes Gateway auth/config semantics and may create a new authorization boundary, so code inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Design native scoped tokens
options.body: Define `gateway.auth.tokens[]` or an equivalent canonical credential model that carries user identity/scopes through Gateway sessions and aligns with #92367 and #68353 before implementation.

options.title: Delegate to proxy/front layer
options.body: Document shared-token mode as single-operator only and direct multi-user deployments to trusted-proxy, separate Gateways, or front-layer tools such as Pinchy.

options.title: Split attribution from authorization
options.body: Handle chat author labeling separately from bearer-token isolation so UI attribution can advance without claiming token-level authorization semantics.

recommendation.title: Design native scoped tokens
recommendation.body: Define `gateway.auth.tokens[]` or an equivalent canonical credential model that carries user identity/scopes through Gateway sessions and aligns with #92367 and #68353 before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history scan points to heavy recent Gateway auth/docs work across the affected files.
